summary: AGPL-3.0 Laravel 12 + React 19/Inertia MES (185 stars, last push 2026-11-04, release 0.28.0 on 2026-11-01) with MQTT and Modbus ingestion in PHP and a Node OPC UA sidecar; OEE is a relational per-line/shift/day percent calculation with no [0,1] clamp, and the README's Vue/Livewire, organization_id, TimescaleDB, Kafka and AI claims do not match the code.

d1_oee.formula: availability = operating_min / (planned_min - planned_downtime_min) x 100, where operating_min = max(0, net_planned - loss_downtime) and loss = unplanned + changeover; performance = (total_produced x ideal_cycle_min / operating_min) x 100, capped at 100 only; quality = (total_produced - scrap) / total_produced x 100; oee = A x P x Q / 10000 (percent scale). Source: backend/app/Services/Production/OeeCalculationService.php
d1_oee.storage: Relational table oee_records (backend/app/Models/OeeRecord.php), upserted per (line_id, shift_id, record_date) with workstation_id always null, written by artisan oee:calculate (backend/app/Console/Commands/CalculateOeeCommand.php, defaults to yesterday). Not a time-series store; no TimescaleDB anywhere in the file tree.
gaps: No clamp on availability or quality: goodProduced = total - scrap is unbounded, so quality goes negative when scrap exceeds produced
Only performance is capped (at 100); OEE is stored as a 0-100 percent, not a [0,1] ratio

Ideal cycle defaults to the fastest completed batch in the last 30 days, so performance is self-referential and near 100 by construction; the manual ideal_cycle_minutes on the template is used only when set
Silent fallback to ideal cycle = 1.0 minute when no template or history exists, producing a meaningless performance figure
The historical ideal-cycle query has a lower date bound (>= date - 30) but no upper bound, so recomputing a past day uses later batches
No per-workstation OEE: calculateForDate always writes workstation_id = null even though the column exists
Machine counters do not feed OEE; production quantity comes only from batches with status DONE

d2_downtime.model: Hybrid. workstation_states is the state timeline (one open row with ended_at NULL; duration_seconds set on close). production_downtimes is a period table that WorkstationStateMachine::transition opens automatically for STOPPED/FAULT/WAITING (unplanned) and CLEANING/MAINTENANCE (planned), with AUTO-STOP/FAULT/WAIT/CLEAN/MAINT reasons. machine_events is an append-only event store (state_change/counter/alarm/telemetry). OFFLINE is not a state; 'No data' is derived from a stale updated_at on the open state row, touched by markSignal() at most once per 60 s. Sources: backend/app/Services/Machine/WorkstationStateMachine.php, backend/app/Models/WorkstationState.php, backend/app/Models/ProductionDowntime.php
schema_fields: production_downtimes: line_id, workstation_id, downtime_reason_id, needs_reason, classified_at, classified_by_id, shift_id, started_at, ended_at, duration_minutes, notes, reported_by, tenant_id
workstation_states: workstation_id, state, started_at, ended_at, duration_seconds, source (machine|manual), metadata JSON
machine_events: workstation_id, machine_connection_id, event_type, state_from, state_to, payload JSON, event_timestamp timestamp(6), correlation_id uuid, synced_to_cloud boolean
gaps: OFFLINE is not an explicit state or transition; it is inferred only from updated_at staleness
Duration rounding is inconsistent: closeDowntimeIfOpen uses ceil(seconds/60) while ProductionDowntime::stop() truncates (int) diffInMinutes
transition() closes any open production_downtime on the station on every state change, including operator-entered downtimes, so a manual reason can be cut short by an automatic transition
Two parallel state-time models (workstation_states and production_downtimes) must be kept in sync by the state machine; no single source of truth
Gateway-supplied ts is trusted for backdating; no clock-skew or ordering policy was evident

protocols: MQTT 3.1.1 via php-mqtt/client: backend/app/Console/Commands/MqttListenCommand.php, one supervisor process reconciling active connections every 5 s, QoS from config, optional TLS with CA
Modbus TCP via aldas/modbus-tcp-client: backend/app/Services/Machine/Modbus/ModbusReader.php (read function codes only), plus ModbusPollCommand
OPC UA via Node.js sidecar opcua-gateway/index.js using node-opcua-client: subscriptions, None or Basic256Sha256, username auth
Generic REST bridge: GET/POST /api/v1/machine-connections/{id}/gateway-config, signals, heartbeat
d3_device.edge_arch: No Rust edge. The only out-of-process edge component is the Node OPC UA sidecar, which is outbound-only (client to OPC UA server, HTTPS POST to API, no inbound port). MQTT and Modbus run inside the PHP app. All adapters funnel into MachineSignalIngestor, which routes to WorkstationStateMachine and MachineCounterService. MQTT messages dispatched as ProcessMqttMessageJob (ShouldQueue, tries=3).
d3_device.write_guard: No machine write-back found: OPC UA gateway only monitors Value attributes, Modbus reader only issues read function codes, and MQTT is subscribe-only. Residual: admin-configured MQTT mappings can mutate MES data via ActionExecutor (update batch step, set work-order status, update line status, create issue, count step, webhook forward). The gateway authenticates with a user-bound Sanctum token.
gaps: OPC UA reconnection: node-opcua connectionStrategy (maxRetry 3) covers only initial connect; no handler for session or subscription loss after run() succeeds
Readings posted fire-and-forget per value change with no retry, buffer or sequence number; API outage loses samples (at-most-once)
Gateway uses long-lived Sanctum user token instead of scoped, rotatable machine key
MQTT TLS CA written to a tempnam() file and never removed (MqttListenCommand.php)
ProcessMqttMessageJob is not idempotent: a retry after MachineMessage::create failure can re-run counter and state actions

d4_data_model.hierarchy: Tenant -> Line -> Workstation (typed by workstation_types); ProcessTemplate -> TemplateSteps; WorkOrder -> Batch -> BatchStep (with lot consumption, step outputs, documents); ProductType, Subassembly, ProcessSegment, BOM items, Material, MaterialLot, SerialUnit, Pallet; Shift (line-scoped or plant-wide).
d4_data_model.shift_model: shifts table (start_time, end_time, days_of_week cast, line_id nullable for plant-wide, is_active). backend/app/Support/ShiftWindow.php computes occurrence windows: when end <= start the window wraps past midnight (addDay); startingOn(shift, date) returns the occurrence. Downtime and production attributed by occurrence start/end rather than calendar date. Overnight attribution has a dedicated test (backend/tests/Feature/Production/OvernightDowntimeAttributionTest.php).
order_states: WorkOrder: PENDING, ACCEPTED, IN_PROGRESS, BLOCKED, PAUSED, CHANGE_HOLD, DONE, REJECTED, CANCELLED
d4_data_model.telemetry_schema: machine_events (append-only; event_type, state_from/state_to, JSON payload, event_timestamp timestamp(6), correlation_id uuid, synced_to_cloud boolean), plus workstation_states and machine_counters / machine_counter_readings. Plain PostgreSQL tables; no hypertable.
d4_data_model.tenancy: Shared schema with tenant_id on rows, not organization_id. TenantScope global scope and HasTenant trait filter and stamp tenant_id; headless API-key requests use a request-scoped TenantContext; nullable tenant_id marks global rows. Tenant-isolation tests exist. Cross-tenant access should surface as 404 via the scope, but test bodies were not read to confirm it.

d5_api.versioning: URL path versioning under /api/v1 (backend/routes/api.php, ~426 Route:: declarations); ERP integrations under /api/v1/erp with API-key auth; OpenAPI generated with dedoc/scramble; human docs in docs/API_DOCUMENTATION.md
d5_api.realtime: Laravel Reverb WebSocket private channels (backend/routes/channels.php: operator-line.{line}, col.{tenant}.{collection}, shift-monitor.{workstation}) consumed with laravel-echo and pusher-js. A server-defined shape sync layer (backend/app/Sync/Shape.php, ShapeRegistry.php) provides a snapshot GET /api/collections/{name} plus delta broadcasts via TanStack DB. No SSE found.
d5_api.envelope: Documented success envelope {data, meta}; lists add pagination meta. Domain events are Laravel events (WorkstationStateChanged, MachineMessageReceived), not a versioned event envelope; no CloudEvents-style schema.
d5_api.auth: Sanctum tokens for /api/v1 (auth:sanctum); login throttled at 10/min; roles via spatie/laravel-permission (Admin, Supervisor, Operator); 2FA via pragmarx/google2fa-laravel. ERP keys: omk_ prefix, SHA-256 hash only, scope allowlist (backend/app/Enums/ApiScope.php), optional IP allowlist, expiry. Unauthenticated POST /api/v1/workstations/register and /heartbeat (LAN-trusted, throttled).

gaps: No AI or LLM layer: no Anthropic, OpenAI or other LLM SDK in backend/composer.json or backend/package.json, and no MCP server or AI tool definitions
Application-level audit trail (backend/app/Traits/Auditable.php) is not an AI audit, and createAuditLog returns early when running in console, so queue jobs leave no audit rows
README claim of PostgreSQL-enforced immutable audit logs is not evidenced: the create_audit_logs migration has no trigger, REVOKE or policy

d7_quality.tests: PHPUnit 11 with ~404 PHP test files under backend/tests (Feature and Unit; Sync, Machine, Connectivity, OEE and tenant-isolation suites). 75 frontend test files run with vitest. Coverage not measured in CI.
d7_quality.ci: .github/workflows/tests.yml: PHP 8.3 and Node 20, composer install, npm ci and build, npm test, then php artisan test --stop-on-failure on SQLite. Other workflows: deploy.yml, docker-publish.yml, release.yml. Tests run on SQLite, not PostgreSQL 17 (the production target).
d7_quality.migrations: 272 migration files in backend/database/migrations, timestamp-named. down() is present in all 4 sampled. The api_keys migration uses raw DB::statement for a partial unique index.
security_flags: Unauthenticated workstation self-registration and heartbeat (relying on LAN trust and rate limiting)
Machine gateway endpoints accept user-bound Sanctum tokens
Audit logging is skipped in console and queue contexts (backend/app/Traits/Auditable.php)
MQTT payloads can trigger admin-configured outbound webhooks (ActionExecutor webhookForward); destination validation (SSRF surface) not verified
MQTT TLS CA written to a temp file and never deleted
d7_quality.last_active: Repo pushed 2026-11-04T21:09:03Z; last main commit 2026-11-01 (release/0.28.0); 185 stars

adopt: Protocol-agnostic ingest facade (MachineSignalIngestor): every adapter normalizes to tag+value, routed by signal_type (state, good/reject/cycle_complete, telemetry, alarm)
Automatic downtime from machine state with per-state planned vs unplanned mapping and needs_reason flag forcing human classification of unexplained stops (WorkstationStateMachine.php)
Heartbeat liveness for on-change protocols: markConnectionSignal keeps a FAULT station from reading as No data
Append-only machine_events with correlation_id and synced_to_cloud, suited to edge-to-cloud replay
Occurrence-based shift windows that attribute stops and output to the shift running across midnight (ShiftWindow.php, OvernightDowntimeAttributionTest)
Hashed API keys with prefix, scope allowlist enum, IP allowlist and expiry, enforced by middleware (ApiKey.php, ApiScope.php)
Server-defined named sync shapes so clients never choose tables or filters (backend/app/Sync/Shape.php)
Tenant-namespaced private channels with explicit authorization (backend/routes/channels.php)
Outbound-only, subscription-based Node OPC UA sidecar (opcua-gateway/index.js)
avoid: Relational OEE upsert per line/shift/day with unbounded quality and no [0,1] clamp, plus self-referential ideal cycle from fastest recent batch
Ceil vs truncate duration rounding in two code paths
Audit writes skipped in console and queue contexts
User-bound long-lived Sanctum tokens as machine credentials
Unauthenticated machine and workstation registration endpoints
Fire-and-forget HTTP posting of readings with no retry, buffer or idempotency key
CI testing only on SQLite while production targets PostgreSQL
differentiate: Rust edge gateway with store-and-forward, idempotent event IDs and sequence numbers (OpenMES gateway is at-most-once HTTP)
Kafka plus Temporal for durable, replayable workflows (OpenMES uses Laravel queues and DB tables)
TimescaleDB hypertables for machine telemetry and OEE time series (OpenMES stores daily aggregates in plain tables)
ISO 22400 OEE with ideal cycle from engineering standards, clamped to [0,1], and per-workstation OEE
Read-only AI investigation layer with approved parameterized tools, tenant-isolated and audited; OpenMES has no AI layer
Explicit OFFLINE detection as a state (OpenMES infers offline from staleness)
Database-enforced tenant isolation (organization_id on every row; OpenMES relies on application-level TenantScope, no RLS policy seen)
